summary: The Research Training Program is how the Australian Government funds research master's and PhD students, domestic and international. The government gives the money to universities, and each university runs its own applications and selection.
meta_description: Australia's Research Training Program pays tuition, a stipend and allowances for research master's and PhD students, including international students.
covers: A stipend for general living costs: the full-time base rate is AUD 35,550 for 2027, and universities may pay up to AUD 55,537.
Allowances for the extra costs of a research degree.
Support for three to four years of full-time doctoral study, or up to two years for a research master's.
eligibility: Domestic and international students admitted to a research doctorate or research master's at an eligible Australian university.
Each university sets its own selection criteria, usually academic results and research potential.
how_to_apply: Choose the university and, ideally, a supervisor for your research.
Apply through that university: the Department of Education does not take applications.
You may apply for RTP scholarships at more than one university.
watch_out: Closing dates differ by university: the University of Sydney's next international round closes on 18 December 2026, the University of Queensland's on 19 October 2026, and ANU's on 15 April 2027.
Some universities pay more than the base stipend: the University of Sydney pays AUD 44,293 a year in 2027.
